clue.text: Main function of church vessel with gold facing

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A church-owned boat trimmed with gold, put to its principal purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine praise and prayer is the chief activity a church exists for.

clue.text: County flags

definitions.meaning: the short form of Wiltshire, an English county
tires or droops, as a flower does without water

explanation.walkthrough: Wiltshire is a county in south-west England, home of Stonehenge.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviated English shire name, and a verb meaning droops or weakens.

clue.text: Having differed, our men will need time to get on again

indicators.note: the letters have become different, rearranged

explanation.surface: Our men fell out and will need a while before they're on good terms again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' suggests getting along; here it is climbing back onto a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount once more, as a rider climbs back into the saddle.

clue.text: Catch consists of plaice, primarily

parts.note: to have is to contain or comprise

indicators.note: taking the word first, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A fisherman's haul is all flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like a haul of fish; it is a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged metal fastening for a door or lid, held by a staple and padlock.

clue.text: Down-to-earth couple in pack unsuited as tricksters

parts.note: sensible and realistic means practical
a pack of cards usually has two jokers, which belong to no suit

explanation.surface: A sensible pair packed off as tricksters despite being ill-matched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsuited' looks like ill-matched; jokers have no suit in a card pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Pranksters who play tricks on people, the phrase for those who stage hoaxes.

clue.text: Passes thin line through series of linked posts

definitions.meaning: as one ... a needle, passing cotton through its eye
online forum conversations, each a chain of replies

explanation.surface: Someone stringing a fine line through a row of connected fence posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'posts' look like fence posts; in the second sense they are internet messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a verb for passing yarn through, and a noun plural for chains of forum messages.

clue.text: Modify mother's offer due to basic human rights

indicators.note: to modify is to alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to change a mother's offer because of fundamental rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modify' rearranges MOTHERS, OFFER and DUE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's 1941 list of essential liberties: speech, worship, and freedom from want and fear.

clue.text: Left-leaning Tory group, say, turning up in a bit of a pickle?

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left
C is short for Conservative
Abba was a Swedish pop group

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A left-wing Conservative faction appears, a bit of a predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' looks like a fix; the question mark flags pickled vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled purple cabbage is one component of a jar of pickles, an example.

clue.text: Leading setter's collected works

parts.note: arch means chief, as in archbishop
the setter has, contracted as 'I've'

explanation.surface: The principal crossword setter's anthology of puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A stored collection of records or documents, kept together.

clue.text: Curvaceous mimic, learner in cast

to ape is to imitate
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A shapely impressionist and a novice appear in a play's cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors; it is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an attractive figure, a well-formed body.

clue.text: Successive notes on fruit showing side effect of hard water

indicators.note: in an across clue the notes placed on the fruit come after it

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a scale is a run of notes in sequence

explanation.surface: Musical notes played in a row about fruit reveal a domestic plumbing nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium deposits furring kettles and pipes are the familiar result of mineral-rich supply.

clue.text: Formal statements from island court received by prosecutor

indicators.note: the island and court are taken inside the prosecutor's letters

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: Official pronouncements from a court on an island are passed to the prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural of a word for an authoritative pronouncement, especially a judge's remark.

clue.text: Singular wordplay concocted

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A lone pun was invented, as if describing a crossword setter's day.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn that is spun is made up, so the past participle means invented.

clue.text: Cricketing pair in standard first-class team withdrew

indicators.note: the cricketing pair is placed within the abbreviation for standard

parts.note: a pair in cricket is two ducks, scores of nought, shown as two Os
A is top grade, as in A1
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricketing pair in a regular top-flight team pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'pair' is being out for nought in both innings, so two noughts; 'in' puts them inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving out of the way, or giving up a post, is a phrasal synonym for retired.

clue.text: Fault in flyers supporting MP overcome by new technology

indicators.note: covered over by, so the rest sits between these two letters

parts.note: IT is information technology

indicators.note: in a down clue the flyers hold up the MP from beneath

parts.note: airmen are pilots, those who fly

explanation.surface: A defect found in pilots backing a politician swamped by modern tech.
explanation.definitionFit: A weakness or damage that reduces how well something works.

clue.text: Type of power US agents tackling annual test reviewed

indicators.note: taken as re-viewed, looked at the other way round, so the whole is read backwards
the agents grapple with the test by holding it within their letters

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
the MOT is the yearly UK roadworthiness check for vehicles

explanation.surface: American agents investigate a yearly test of some form of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's compulsory annual vehicle safety test. 'tackling' holds the test within the agents' letters, and 'reviewed' turns the whole round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is often described by this adjective, as in a nuclear power station.

clue.text: Resilient component of bridge close to motorway

parts.note: a rubber is a unit of play in the card game bridge

indicators.note: the close, or end, of a word supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: A sturdy part of a road bridge sits near the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge looks like a structure; it is the card game, where a rubber is a best-of-three set of games.
explanation.definitionFit: Springy and elastic, bouncing back like the stretchy material it names.

clue.text: Artist's 'Old Witch' in demand

definitions.note: read as 'artist is', the 's being the verb

indicators.note: the witch is placed within the word for demand

parts.note: a call is a demand, as in calls for change
a hag is an ugly old woman or witch

explanation.surface: A painter's work titled 'Old Witch' is much sought after.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter famous for dreamlike village scenes.

clue.text: Accountant set up country's legal system, in part

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means read upwards

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK

explanation.surface: An accountant establishes part of a nation's legal framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' looks like establish; it turns WALES upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Law built from judges' previous rulings, one strand of a common-law system.

clue.text: Grecian urn of lead-free pungent mineral on core of alabaster

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second
without its leading letter

parts.note: camphor is a strong-smelling crystalline substance

indicators.note: the centre letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Greek vase made of strongly scented stone on an alabaster centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-handled jar of ancient Greece used for wine or oil.

clue.text: Very good south coast resort out of bounds

indicators.note: with its bounds, the outer letters, removed

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A seaside resort on the south coast is declared off-limits, and that's fine.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a resort town in Sussex; 'out of bounds' strips its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful British interjection of assent, like 'okay' or 'fine'.

clue.text: Small rock singer bringing in millions

indicators.note: the singer takes the millions inside

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano
M stands for million

explanation.surface: A minor rock star earns millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock singer' looks like a pop star, but 'Small rock' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake or quiver slightly, a gentle rocking.

clue.text: Eg USSR's renewed purpose when ethnic revolt starts

definitions.note: the 's is 'is': the Soviet Union is an example

indicators.note: made new, so these letters are rearranged
the starts of the three words supply their opening letters

explanation.surface: The Soviet Union's purpose revived once ethnic uprisings began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewed' rearranges PURPOSE into SUPERPO; 'starts' adds W, E, R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet Union was one of two dominant world powers during the Cold War.

clue.text: Be awed by sound of German quartet?

indicators.note: what is heard when the German word is said

parts.note: vier is the German for four

explanation.surface: Being impressed by a German string quartet's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: German 'vier' is said 'fear'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand in awe of, as in fearing God, is to revere.

clue.text: Hairy rebellious Irish broadcaster

indicators.note: rising up in revolt, so in a down clue read upwards

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: An unkempt, defiant Irish presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' looks literal; it is slang for dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a frightening or dangerous situation is described as hair-raising.

clue.text: Western worker's deficiency

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A cowboy labourer's shortcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack or absence of something needed.

clue.text: Earl pursuing several ladies, perhaps of doubtful morals

indicators.note: the earl follows behind, so comes after

explanation.surface: A nobleman chasing a string of women, perhaps not the most virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' looks like women; in Britain it is also the women's lavatory, a LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing promiscuous behaviour, an older sense of lax or immoral.

clue.text: M Antony's friend, one reversing vehicle behind obstruction

indicators.note: the vehicle comes after the obstruction
the word one is turned back to front

parts.note: a bar is a barrier or obstruction
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: One backing a vehicle up behind a roadblock, attributed to Mark Antony's companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns ONE into ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony's loyal officer in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, who deserts him.

clue.text: Passion finally erupts when Nutmeg's drunk spirits

indicators.note: taken in, swallowed, so the setter goes inside the passion

parts.note: wrath is passionate anger
the setter Nutmeg refers to themself as I, the 's being 'is'

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Anger boils over once the setter has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutmeg's drunk' reads as 'I is drunk': I is swallowed by WRATH, and 'finally' adds the S that ends 'erupts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts or apparitions are called spirits, as are drinks, which the surface plays on.

clue.text: More than enough from composer, totally drained

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer

indicators.note: emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A composer has had his fill, completely worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being sated, having had a surfeit of food or anything else.
